summary: The sample implements the core starter-prompt goals: a Node.js + Mongoose multi-tenant storefront with shared collections, tenantId on every schema, tenant-scoped compound indexes, a repository layer and a defensive tenant-safety plugin. The build ran seed, verify-indexes and the isolation test against the live cluster and validated the compound indexes via the MCP tool. Findings: (1) the seed is not fully idempotent (orders are created unconditionally), (2) the seed and test sometimes bypass the repository layer, (3) no explicit retry/backoff logic was added for transient/429 throttles although connection guidance was consulted, and (4) a handful of gallery expectations (IaC, unit tests without a live cluster, and a more complete .env.example) remain incomplete. Several expected DocumentDB practices are discoverable and were followed (connection reuse, tenant-leading indexes, reading connection string from env, not committing secrets). Two multi-tenant practices (centralized repository-plugin enforcement and automated tests that assert blocking of dangerous repo ops) are prior_knowledge-only in the public guidance and are therefore things the product docs/agent kit should publish to avoid agents inventing them.

requirement_results.requirement: A Node.js application uses Mongoose as its ODM against Azure DocumentDB and stores merchant products, orders and inventory in collections shared by all merchants, one collection per resource (e.g. products, orders, inventory) holding every tenant's documents.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/product.js (lines 4-11 define Product schema); app/src/models/index.js (lines 6-8) registers Product/Inventory/Order models which create collections 'products', 'inventories', 'orders'.

requirement_results.requirement: The Mongoose schemas for products, orders and inventory each define a tenantId field, and every document written through the application carries a tenantId value.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/product.js (line 5), app/src/models/inventory.js (line 5), app/src/models/order.js (line 5) define tenantId; repo methods set tenantId (app/src/repos/productRepo.js line 10, app/src/repos/orderRepo.js line 9, app/src/repos/inventoryRepo.js update uses $setOnInsert with tenantId).

requirement_results.requirement: A compound index on (tenantId, sku), with tenantId as the leading key, is defined in application code (e.g. schema.index({ tenantId: 1, sku: 1 })) on the shared collection(s) that carry a sku field.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/product.js (line 15) ProductSchema.index({ tenantId: 1, sku: 1 }, { unique: true }); app/src/models/inventory.js (line 12) InventorySchema.index({ tenantId: 1, sku: 1 }).

requirement_results.requirement: A compound index on (tenantId, createdAt), with tenantId as the leading key, is defined in application code (e.g. schema.index({ tenantId: 1, createdAt: 1 })) on the shared collection(s) that carry a createdAt field.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/order.js (line 19) OrderSchema.index({ tenantId: 1, createdAt: -1 });

requirement_results.requirement: A repository layer sits between the rest of the application and the Mongoose models, and all reads and writes of products, orders and inventory go through it.
requirement_results.evidence: Repository classes exist: app/src/repos/productRepo.js, inventoryRepo.js, orderRepo.js. However, seed.js writes documents directly via mongoose models (app/src/seed.js lines 25-31 perform Product.findOneAndUpdate, Inventory.updateOne and Order.create without using repos). tests/isolation.test.js also calls Product model directly to set up tenantB fixture (tests/isolation.test.js line 14).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Change src/seed.js and tests/isolation.test.js to instantiate and call the appropriate repository methods (e.g., new ProductRepo(models, tenant).createOrUpdate(...)) so all reads/writes go through the repo.

requirement_results.requirement: Every repository read method includes tenantId as an equality condition in the query filter it passes to Mongoose.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/repos/productRepo.js findBySku uses { tenantId: this.tenantId, sku } (line 15-16); listAll uses { tenantId: this.tenantId } (lines 19-20). app/src/repos/orderRepo.js listRecent uses { tenantId: this.tenantId } (line 14-15). app/src/repos/inventoryRepo.js getInventory uses { tenantId: this.tenantId, sku } (line 14-15).

requirement_results.requirement: Every repository update and delete method includes tenantId in its filter alongside the document selector (e.g. { _id, tenantId }), so a write only touches documents of that tenant.
requirement_results.evidence: Update/upsert methods include tenantId: productRepo.findOneAndUpdate filter uses { tenantId, sku } (app/src/repos/productRepo.js line 11-12); inventoryRepo.updateOne uses { tenantId, sku } (app/src/repos/inventoryRepo.js line 9-11). There are no delete methods implemented to inspect.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If deletes are required by the sample, add repository delete methods that include tenantId in the filter (e.g., deleteById(id) that uses { _id: id, tenantId }).

requirement_results.requirement: Repository methods take the tenant identity from a tenant context supplied to the repository (e.g. a constructor argument or per-call parameter) and add the tenantId condition to the filter themselves.
requirement_results.evidence: All repository constructors require tenantId: productRepo constructor checks tenantId (app/src/repos/productRepo.js line 2-5), inventoryRepo and orderRepo similarly (app/src/repos/inventoryRepo.js line 2-6; app/src/repos/orderRepo.js line 2-6).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/mongoose.js reads process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI (lines 4-7) and throws if missing. .env.example contains a placeholder only (app/.env.example). No credentials are hard-coded in source files.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example documents DOCUMENTDB_URI placeholder (line 1) but does not include optional settings such as PORT referenced in README or other runtime knobs.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add other commonly used runtime settings (e.g., PORT) to .env.example with placeholders.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector indexes or embeddings are created or used in this sample.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector indexes are used in the code or README.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/mongoose.js implements a singleton-style connect() with an isConnected guard and exports the mongoose instance; server calls connect() but the same connection is reused (src/mongoose.js lines 12-19).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js (lines 14-17) runs createIndexes() idempotently and products/inventory are upserted (lines 25-29). However Order.create(...) at line 31 will create a new order each run (not idempotent).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Change the Order creation to an upsert (e.g., findOneAndUpdate with upsert: true keyed by tenantId+orderNumber) or check for existence before creating.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: No /search endpoint is present in app/src/server.js.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If search is part of the sample, add a /search handler that validates input, returns 400 for empty queries, and reports embedding errors with an explanatory 5xx message.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search implementation exists to check.

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: This is a Node project: package-lock.json is committed (app/package-lock.json) providing reproducible installs. package.json lists semver ranges (app/package.json lines 16-20) and package-lock.json pins transitive dependencies.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: tests/isolation.test.js explicitly connects to the live cluster referenced by DOCUMENTDB_URI and the test runs against the live DB (tests/isolation.test.js line 1 comment and test body lines 6-12).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Provide unit tests that mock Mongoose (e.g., using sinon or in-memory gateway) or add instructions and a script to run tests against the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image for local CI-free runs.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC files (Bicep/ARM/Terraform) are present in the repository. The builder logged a decision not to provision (decisions.jsonl D005/D006).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a Bicep (or Terraform) template that targets Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters for tier, region and storage (example quickstart templates exist in the product docs).

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md includes What it shows, Prerequisites, Quickstart steps (lines 3-18) and Cleanup guidance (lines 28-29).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md (line 1) uses 'Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB wire protocol)'; .env.example host matches mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com. No neighbouring product names appear.

checks.practice: Always require TLS on client connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/src/mongoose.js reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and passes it unchanged to mongoose.connect (line 17); .env.example suggests mongodb+srv with tls=true (app/.env.example).

checks.practice: Create one MongoClient/Mongoose connection and reuse it (singleton pattern); do not open a new connection per request and tune the connection pool for your hosting model (serverless vs long-running).
checks.evidence: app/src/mongoose.js implements connect() with an isConnected guard and exports the mongoose instance (lines 12-19). server.js calls connect() for incoming requests but uses the shared connection.

checks.practice: Treat 429 (Request Rate Too Large) and server transient errors as retryable and implement exponential backoff/retry logic while monitoring RU usage to reduce throttling.
checks.evidence: Code contains no retry/backoff wrappers around repository operations or global retry policies. e.g., productRepo.createOrUpdate simply calls findOneAndUpdate (app/src/repos/productRepo.js line 11-12).
checks.fix: Wrap ephemeral data-plane operations in an exponential-backoff retry helper that retries on 429 and transient network errors; add a note in README about monitoring throttling and RU/compute considerations.

checks.practice: Use the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) when designing compound indexes and prefer a single well-shaped compound index over several single-field indexes.
checks.evidence: Indexes use tenantId as leading key for sku and createdAt: ProductSchema.index({ tenantId: 1, sku: 1 }) (app/src/models/product.js line 15), OrderSchema.index({ tenantId: 1, createdAt: -1 }) (app/src/models/order.js line 19).

checks.practice: Read the cluster connection string from environment or a secrets store at runtime (do not commit credentials to repo); in production use Azure Key Vault or managed identity-based secrets instead of plain env vars.
checks.evidence: app/src/mongoose.js reads process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI and .env.example contains a placeholder (app/.env.example, src/mongoose.js lines 4-7). No connection strings are committed.

checks.practice: Create indexes idempotently during deployment or as an off-peak job and avoid creating large indexes synchronously on production under heavy load.
checks.evidence: src/seed.js calls Product.createIndexes(), Inventory.createIndexes() and Order.createIndexes() (app/src/seed.js lines 14-17) before seeding; createIndexes is idempotent. The seed uses upserts for most sample data.

checks.practice: When running seeds or migrations, make scripts idempotent and safe to run repeatedly and create indexes and sample data with upserts or existence checks.
checks.evidence: Seed uses upserts for products and inventory (app/src/seed.js lines 25-29) but creates orders with Order.create(...) (app/src/seed.js line 31) which will insert duplicates when run multiple times.
checks.fix: Change the Order creation to an upsert keyed by (tenantId, orderNumber) or use findOneAndUpdate with upsert:true.

checks.practice: After creating or changing indexes as part of deployment, verify index state with getIndexes()/list_indexes and re-run explain to confirm queries now use the intended index.
checks.evidence: The repo includes src/verify_indexes.js that lists collection.indexes() and the build ran documentdb.list_indexes via MCP for products/inventories/orders (events logged tool output lines 40-44), confirming the intended compound indexes exist.

checks.practice: Require a tenantId equality predicate on every read/write operation and enforce it centrally (e.g., a Mongoose repository-layer plugin that injects { tenantId } into queries and rejects any operation that would run without it).
checks.evidence: The sample includes a tenantSafetyPlugin that rejects queries without tenantId (app/src/models/tenantSafetyPlugin.js lines 9-16) and repository constructors require tenantId (app/src/repos/* constructors).
checks.what_would_help: A public Azure DocumentDB page showing an example Mongoose plugin or snippet that rejects tenant-less queries would let an agent find and reuse this pattern without relying on prior knowledge.

checks.practice: Detect and block dangerous repository operations (e.g., updateMany, deleteMany without tenantId) via code review or automated tests; include unit/integration tests that assert tenant isolation (queries cannot return results from other tenantIds).
checks.evidence: The tenantSafetyPlugin aborts operations missing tenantId and the tests/isolation.test.js checks the plugin blocks a query without tenantId (tests/isolation.test.js lines 24-32).
checks.what_would_help: A public guidance page with recommended test patterns and a canonical plugin snippet (for Mongoose/Azure DocumentDB) would prevent agents from inventing custom approaches.

checks.practice: Do not hardcode admin passwords or connection strings in code or parameter files; reference secrets from Azure Key Vault in deployment templates and read connection strings from the environment or a secrets store at runtime.
checks.evidence: No secrets are committed; connection string read from process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI and .env.example contains only a placeholder (app/src/mongoose.js lines 4-7, app/.env.example).

decision_reviews.comment: D001 recorded an operator approval with 'ready_with_gaps'. This is an operator action and the events show the build proceeded; the reason 'Approved with --yes' is an operator-supplied rationale and is consistent with the build trace.
D002: Choosing Node.js + Mongoose with Express is justified by the prompt. The events show Node/Express files and a server were written and used (events show write_file for src/server.js and tests).

D003 chose Mongoose ^7.4.0 by model_default. The build did record that choice (package.json created with mongoose ^7.4.0) but the readiness notes and some Microsoft quickstarts reference newer Mongoose examples; the decision_source is 'model_default' rather than a documentation citation. The choice is defensible but not clearly aligned with the public quickstart recommendation; consider pinning to a documented tested version or citing the docs. Evidence: events show package.json created with ^7.4.0 (events.write_file at timestamp 05:40:37 and 05:40:39).
D004 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from env. The code implements this (src/mongoose.js lines 4-7), and events show that being used during connect and tests; this is consistent with guidance and run-policy.

D005 refused to provision Azure resources because run policy forbids Azure writes. The events and the repository contain no IaC; the build used an existing cluster via the connection profile and DOCUMENTDB_URI as required. The decision is supported by the run environment.

D006: The builder chose not to set a shard key because sharding would require provisioning and cluster-level changes. Given the run policy and the sample goals (repository-layer tenant isolation and tenant-leading indexes), this is a practical choice and is reflected in the code (no sharding code or IaC).

D007: Enforcing tenant isolation in the repository and adding a Mongoose safety plugin was implemented (app/src/repos/* and app/src/models/tenantSafetyPlugin.js). The events show the plugin was created and tested (isolation.test.js exercised the plugin).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A public Azure DocumentDB page or quickstart that documents and publishes a canonical Mongoose 'tenant safety' plugin pattern (inject tenantId into queries and reject tenant-less operations).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Loaded documentdb skills, searched Azure docs and the agent-kit; found the pattern as prior knowledge only (discovered_practices K01, K19 are prior_knowledge_only).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder nevertheless implemented a plugin from prior knowledge; however, agents that lacked this memory might not invent the defensively-safe pattern and could produce samples that allow cross-tenant queries.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short docs page titled 'Enforcing tenant isolation in Mongoose' with: (1) rationale; (2) canonical plugin code snippet that rejects query/update/delete middleware lacking tenantId; (3) how to apply the plugin to schemas and integrate with repository constructors; (4) a small test pattern that asserts a query without tenantId throws. Include copy-paste examples and a link from the Mongoose quickstart.

doc_gaps.topic: Guidance and example for seeding idempotently (orders)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: While the local-deployment skill documents idempotent seeds in general, a concrete sample pattern for order-like resources (unique on tenantId+orderNumber) was not in the sample docs. The builder partially implemented idempotent upserts for products/inventory but left Order.create non-idempotent.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-local-deployment skill and index/seed docs; repository code inspection.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Seed is only partially idempotent: running the seed repeatedly creates duplicate Order documents.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short subsection to the seed quickstart: 'Making seeds idempotent' with examples for using findOneAndUpdate/upsert keyed by tenantId+natural-key (e.g., orderNumber), and recommend using bulkWrite for larger datasets. Provide the exact code snippet to replace Order.create with a findOneAndUpdate upsert.

doc_gaps.topic: Recommendation for retry/backoff patterns for Node/Mongoose clients
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The agent-kit lists retry guidance, but there is no small, copy-paste Node/Mongoose retry helper that shows how to wrap repository operations and handle 429/Retry-After using exponential backoff.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-connection and documentdb-driver skills; quickstarts and sample code.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder did not implement retry/backoff logic; absent a concise example, sample authors may omit retries and be vulnerable to transient throttling or transient network errors.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a one-page snippet 'Handling 429 and transient errors' for Node: include a small retry wrapper (Promise-based) that checks MongoError codes and 429, honors Retry-After when present, and uses exponential backoff with jitter. Show how to integrate it at the repository layer.

doc_gaps.topic: Pinning recommended driver versions in quickstart
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A clear single-line recommendation in the Mongoose quickstart that states the tested/pinned driver version to use with the shown code (e.g., 'Use Mongoose 9.12.1 with MongoDB driver X for these docs').
doc_gaps.where_searched: Mongoose quickstart and Azure DocumentDB Node.js examples; readiness notes showed mixed signals about suggested version.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder chose Mongoose ^7.4.0 by model_default (decision D003). This diverges from newer quickstart examples and may cause subtle incompatibilities or confusion for readers about which driver version was tested with the sample.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Tested driver versions' box to the Node/Mongoose quickstart that lists the exact Mongoose and underlying mongodb-driver versions used to validate examples (and the Node.js engine version).

doc_gaps.topic: Canonical guidance for local test runs (DocumentDB Gateway image usage)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short, highlighted snippet in the Mongoose quickstart showing the exact docker-compose or docker run invocation for the DocumentDB Gateway image (port 10260, TLS details) and how to run tests against it.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: tests/isolation.test.js run against the live cluster. Authors wanting offline-only CI or reproducible developer runs need a documented, one-line recipe to run tests locally without a live cluster.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a minimal docker-compose snippet in the quickstart and a 'Testing without cloud' section that shows how to set DOCUMENTDB_URI to point to the Gateway image, supply the certificate, and run npm test. Include an example env file for local runs.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The sample .env.example only lists DOCUMENTDB_URI. A consistent convention and a short manifest of env variables (PORT, NODE_ENV, LOG_LEVEL) would help agents and builders produce full .env.example files.
doc_gaps.where_searched: repo .env.example and README; no centralized guidance found for sample env conventions.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The .env.example omitted PORT and other knobs; readers may be uncertain which env vars are required or optional.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A one-paragraph rule for sample starters: include DOCUMENTDB_URI plus typical runtime env placeholders (PORT, NODE_ENV, LOG_LEVEL) in .env.example. Provide a minimal template to copy into projects.
